good: Trailer shows rival flips, sparks, and three takedowns.
Clear speed, boost, and takedown HUD reacts.
Visible bends and a consistent chase camera.
bad: Scripted play spends most frames crawling against the barrier.
Drift and boost fail to restore useful movement in the controls test.
Boxy cars, repeated cone trees, and flat lighting look basic.
gpt-6.1-sol-high.one_line: The takedowns look fun in the trailer, but the filmed drive mostly shows a car stuck scraping the wall.

good: Takedown beat is genuinely Burnout: huge TAKEDOWN! text, RIVAL WRECKED badge, sparks, counter ticks 0 to 3, boost refills
Trailer proves real speed and drift - 271 to 398 km/h through bending corners with the chase cam locked behind the car
HUD is straight out of Burnout: big KM/H bottom-right, segmented boost bar, takedowns counter, rival gap readout
bad: Filmed drive is a brick: car sits at 2-12 km/h for 40 s with W held and never recovers after the 24 s crash
Rival stays 1 km+ ahead for the whole scripted film, so the duel the brief is built around never happens
Box car, cone trees, flat untextured primitives - generic low-poly Three.js demo look
step-5-preview.one_line: The trailer sells a fun little Burnout-alike with punchy takedowns, but the moment the benchmark script actually drives it the car becomes a 3 km/h brick and the rival just drives away.

good: Trailer shows real wall-slam takedowns with big TAKEDOWN! text, wreck, and smoke
HUD looks like Burnout: big italic speed, segmented boost bar, takedown count, rival gap
Road has bends, chevron signs, and red-white barriers; sunset low-poly scene is clean
bad: In the filmed drive the car rides into the barrier at the first bend and stays stuck at 2-11 km/h for about 50 s
Rival gets 3 km ahead and is never caught, so the drive shows no takedown
Steer, drift, and boost show no effect while the car is pinned to the wall
opus-5.5.one_line: The trailer looks like a fun mini-Burnout, but when I played it I got stuck on the first wall and watched the rival drive off.

good: HUD is genuinely Burnout-shaped: huge speedo, segmented boost bar, takedown counter and rival gap
Takedown is readable and punchy - giant TAKEDOWN! banner, wrecked rival, counter 0-1-2-3, boost refilled
Winding barrier-lined road with real bends, and the camera stays locked behind the car
bad: In the filmed free play the car crawls at 2-12 km/h with W held, so speed and drift feel mostly don't come through
Flat low-poly cone-tree world is cohesive but thin and generic, nothing like Burnout's sense of place
Takedown banner scales up so large it smears across the whole screen in the trailer
deepseek-v4.1-flash.one_line: It looks and reads like Burnout on the HUD, but the car spends the filmed drive stuck at walking pace, so the speed and drift never actually sell.

good: Punchy TAKEDOWN! with flying wreck and boost refill
Cohesive sunset world with barriers, trees, chevrons
Burnout-style HUD with speed, boost, rival distance
bad: Scripted run stuck crawling at 2-5 km/h after wall hit
No visible drift angle in drift test
Boxy cars and flat lighting look cheap up close
muse-spark-1.3-contributor.one_line: Fast and punchy when it gets going, but tap a wall and you crawl.
